title: Team and project dashboards
blurb: Explain which reports the team and project dashboards replace, what goes on them, where they are reviewed, and why information is pulled rather than pushed.
question: In a PRINCE2 Agile project, which artifact can replace the checkpoint report, and where is it reviewed?

teach.body: PRINCE2 Agile tailors two progress reports into visual, always-current dashboards. The team dashboard takes the place of the checkpoint report. The project dashboard takes the place of the highlight report and the end stage report. Rather than someone writing and sending a report at set intervals, the dashboard is kept up to date and the people who need information pull it when they need it.

A team dashboard is continuously updated and reviewed during the team planning and team retrospective workshops, which keeps the team's work transparent; the project manager extracts information as needed. In managing product delivery the team updates it when evaluating a work package, and in controlling a stage the project manager pulls progress from it. A team skill matrix used for a delivery team is also best shown on its dashboard.
teach.cite: PRINCE2 Agile V2 book Table 12.1, Table 13.9, Table 13.12, 7.4.1

teach.body: The project dashboard is a visual picture of the project for the board. It typically shows the release status or plan, burn charts, current risks and issues, the communication plan, and Agilometer or agile assessment trends. It is created in the project kickoff workshop, then continuously updated and reviewed in progress review workshops. In 'report highlights' the project manager assembles the team dashboards, project log and release map changes and updates it so the board can pull what it needs.
teach.cite: PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 12.3.2.1, Table 12.1, Table 13.8, Table 13.9

teach.body: The project kickoff workshop includes a 'team dashboards' topic, aimed at transparency on team activities, accountability and quick insight into team progress and productivity, and a 'project dashboard' topic. Team dashboards are co-created within each team rather than imposed by the project manager, in keeping with self-management. Project support helps meet everyone's reporting needs by updating and pulling information from the dashboards.

teach.body: Lowther Engineering is replacing its maintenance scheduling system with three teams. In the kickoff workshop each team designs its own team dashboard: a burn-down, its skill matrix and blockers. Project manager Hannah Price no longer asks product owners for weekly checkpoint emails; she pulls what she needs from the dashboards. Project support officer Dev Mistry helps keep the project dashboard current, and executive Ruth Elland opens it before each progress review instead of waiting for a highlight report.

teach.text: Do not swap the pairs. TEAM dashboard = checkpoint report (team to PM, reviewed in team planning and retrospectives). PROJECT dashboard = highlight report and end stage report (PM to board, reviewed in progress reviews). And a project manager who dictates every team's dashboard design undermines self-management: teams co-create their own.

items: Team dashboard replaces the checkpoint report; project dashboard replaces the highlight and end stage reports.
Team dashboard: reviewed in team planning and retrospectives; the PM extracts information as needed.
Project dashboard: release status, burn charts, risks and issues, communication plan, Agilometer trends.
Project dashboard is created in the kickoff workshop and reviewed in progress review workshops.
Information is pulled from dashboards rather than pushed in reports.
Teams co-create their own dashboards; project support updates and pulls information.

summary: You can now say which reports the team and project dashboards replace, what a project dashboard shows and where each dashboard is reviewed. You can also explain why dashboards are pulled rather than pushed and co-created by the teams.

A.q: Which artifact can replace the checkpoint report in a PRINCE2 Agile project?
A.why: Table 12.1: the checkpoint report can be replaced by a team dashboard.

whyNot.0: The project dashboard replaces the highlight and end stage reports.
whyNot.2: The release map is the agile form of the project and stage plans.
whyNot.3: The product backlog replaces product descriptions.

A.q: Where is the project dashboard continuously updated and reviewed?
A.why: Table 12.1: the project dashboard is continuously updated and reviewed during progress review workshops.

whyNot.0: Team retrospectives review the team dashboard, not the project dashboard.
whyNot.1: Team planning workshops review the team dashboard.
whyNot.3: The project canvas workshop builds the project canvas in starting up.

A.q: Which management products can the project dashboard replace?
options: Lessons report and end project report
Highlight report and end stage report
A.why: The project dashboard is the agile form of both the highlight report and the end stage report (Table 12.1).

whyNot.0: The checkpoint report is replaced by the team dashboard; the team plan stays a team plan.
whyNot.1: Exception and issue reports remain separate products.
whyNot.2: Lessons and end project reports remain separate products.

B.q: Which would you expect to see on a project dashboard?
options: Release status, burn charts and current risks
Each developer's task list for the day ahead
The full text of every user story
B.why: 12.3.2.1: the project dashboard shows release status or plan, burn charts, current risks and issues, the communication plan and Agilometer or agile assessment trends.

whyNot.1: Daily task lists belong to the team's own planning, not the board's view.
whyNot.2: User stories live in the backlogs; the dashboard summarizes progress.
whyNot.3: Personal appraisals are not dashboard content.

B.q: A project manager designs one dashboard layout and instructs every team to use it unchanged. Why is this not in line with PRINCE2 Agile?
options: Team dashboards are owned by project assurance
Team dashboards are co-created within each team
Team dashboards are designed by the agile coach
Team dashboards are set by the board at initiation
B.why: Team dashboards are not dictated but co-created within the respective teams, supporting self-management (13.4.4.2).

whyNot.0: Project assurance monitors adherence; it does not own team dashboards.
whyNot.2: The agile coach works at organization level on systemic blockers, not on team dashboard design.
whyNot.3: The board pulls information from the project dashboard; it does not design team dashboards.

B.q: Which role helps manage reporting needs by updating and pulling information from project and team dashboards?
B.why: Table B.1: project support helps manage reporting requirements for all stakeholders by updating and pulling information from project and team dashboards.

whyNot.0: Project assurance monitors adherence to principles and practices; it is not an administrative role.
whyNot.1: The team coach helps teams self-manage and facilitates team workshops.
whyNot.2: The CPO owns the project backlog and sets priorities across teams.

C.q: In which process and activity does the project manager update the project dashboard so that the board can pull up-to-date information?
options: Managing product delivery, evaluate a work package
Directing a project, give ongoing direction
Initiating a project, assemble the PID
C.why: Report highlights (controlling a stage): the PM assembles team dashboards, project log and release map revisions, and updates the project dashboard for the board to pull (Table 13.9).

whyNot.0: In evaluate a work package the TEAM updates the TEAM dashboard.
whyNot.2: Give ongoing direction is the board using the dashboard, not the PM updating it.
whyNot.3: The project dashboard is set up in initiation, but highlights are reported during controlling a stage.

C.q:
Which two statements about team dashboards are correct?
1. They are reviewed during team planning and retrospective workshops.
2. They replace the highlight report sent to the board.
3. The project manager extracts information from them as needed.
4. They are reviewed mainly in progress review workshops.
C.why: Table 12.1: the team dashboard is updated and reviewed in team planning and retrospective workshops (1), and the PM extracts information as needed (3).

whyNot.0: Statement 2 is wrong: the highlight report is replaced by the project dashboard.
whyNot.1: Both are wrong: they describe the project dashboard.
whyNot.2: Statement 4 is wrong: progress review workshops review the project dashboard.

C.q: In which workshop are the team dashboards and the project dashboard first set up, and in which process?
options: Project kickoff workshop, initiating a project
Starting up workshop, starting up a project
Release planning workshop, managing a stage boundary
Progress review workshop, controlling a stage
C.why: The project kickoff workshop (initiating a project) includes 'team dashboards' and 'project dashboard' topics; the project dashboard is created there (Table 13.8).

whyNot.1: The starting up workshop covers roles, lessons, initiation stage planning, risk analysis and refining planning.
whyNot.2: The release planning workshop covers OKR definition and updating the release map.
whyNot.3: Progress reviews use the project dashboard; they do not first create it.

reteach.title: The kitchen whiteboard
reteach.question: Why does a family whiteboard beat everyone texting updates?

blocks.body: Each child keeps their own corner of the kitchen whiteboard current: homework done, clubs this week. A parent glances at it when they need to know (pulled), rather than everyone sending texts at set times (pushed). The fridge calendar, kept by a parent, sums up the whole household for visiting grandparents. Corners are team dashboards; the fridge calendar is the project dashboard.

blocks.text: Each child designs their own corner: team dashboards are co-created, not dictated.

explain.body: Checkpoint report becomes team dashboard. Highlight report and end stage report become project dashboard (Table 12.1).

test.q: Identify the missing word in the following sentence. In PRINCE2 Agile, the highlight report can be replaced by the [?] dashboard.
test.why: The project dashboard replaces the highlight report (and the end stage report) (Table 12.1).

whyNot.0: The team dashboard replaces the checkpoint report.
whyNot.1: There is a release map, not a release dashboard, among the named artifacts.
whyNot.3: There is no iteration dashboard among the named artifacts.

explain.body: Team dashboard: team planning and retrospective workshops. Project dashboard: progress review workshops (Table 12.1).

test.q: In which workshops is the team dashboard continuously updated and reviewed?
options: Progress review and project closure workshops
test.why: Table 12.1: the team dashboard is updated and reviewed during team planning and retrospective workshops.

whyNot.0: Progress reviews and the closure workshop deal with the project dashboard.
whyNot.2: Kickoff sets dashboards up and release planning covers OKRs and the release map; neither is the ongoing team review.
whyNot.3: The agile enablement workshop is for the board and agile coaches in directing a project.

explain.body: Teams keep their dashboards current; the PM pulls from them and updates the project dashboard; the board pulls from that (Table 13.9, Table 13.12).

test.q: How does information typically reach the project board in a PRINCE2 Agile project?
options: Teams send checkpoint reports to the board
The board pulls it from the project dashboard
Product owners brief the board weekly
The agile coach compiles a monthly summary
test.why: The PM updates the project dashboard so the board can pull the up-to-date information it needs (Table 13.9).

whyNot.0: Checkpoint information goes from team to PM, via the team dashboard, not to the board.
whyNot.2: There is no standard weekly briefing from POs to the board.
whyNot.3: The agile coach removes systemic blockers; it does not compile progress summaries.

explain.body: Release status or plan, burn charts, current risks and issues, the communication plan, and Agilometer or agile assessment trends (12.3.2.1).

test.q: Which item is typically part of the project dashboard?
options: The project manager's daily log entries
test.why: 12.3.2.1 lists Agilometer or agile assessment trends among the project dashboard's contents.

whyNot.0: The delegation matrix clarifies decision-making authority; it is not listed as dashboard content.
whyNot.1: The daily log is the PM's informal record, not dashboard content.
whyNot.3: Work package descriptions are sets of user stories agreed between PM and PO.
